text: In the EU, lactic acid bacteria sour the low-fat liquid left from churning sweet cream, thickening it slightly and giving it a fresh tang. Its high content of fat-globule membrane (lecithin) makes the flavour change quickly, so it has a short shelf life. In the US and Canada, buttermilk is usually cultured buttermilk: skim or low-fat milk is soured with a mesophilic aroma culture and never churned.

processing.text: EU buttermilk is the low-fat liquid left from churning sweet cream, soured; US and Canadian cultured buttermilk is skim or low-fat milk soured with a mesophilic aroma culture, never churned.
